meta.benchmarkSuite: FIGM Empirical Evaluation Benchmark Testbed v1.0
meta.ruleCoverageNote: 50/50 canonical rules have empirical ground-truth coverage as of this revision (up from 33/33, 25/25, before that 8/25). The most recent 17 rules (FIGM-NEXT-07..10, FIGM-VUE-03..06, FIGM-ANG-07..10, FIGM-REACT-07..11) were added in a second research-backed expansion pass -- see docs/research/EXPANSION_2_RESEARCH_TRACEABILITY.md, including 3 candidates replaced and 1 corrected after research contradicted or duplicated the original brief. Each got one new flat single-rule fixture, following the exact same isolated-single-rule convention as every prior fixture in this testbed (React09Benchmark.jsx deliberately uses fetch() rather than localStorage.setItem to avoid an incidental, disclosed co-fire with the existing FIGM-PERF-06; Ang07/08/09/10 all include changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush to avoid incidentally co-firing FIGM-ANG-02). FIGM-VUE-03..06 are the first Vue rules with REAL_AST detection (via <script>-block extraction and re-parse with the same TypeScript compiler every other real-AST rule uses -- no @vue/compiler-sfc dependency required). Correction (Phase: Vue template real-AST upgrade): FIGM-VUE-01/02 also now have REAL_AST detection, via a dedicated @vue/compiler-dom template parser (src/ast/vue-template-ast-builder.ts) added once package-registry access allowed installing @vue/compiler-dom/@vue/compiler-sfc -- see src/matrix/four-layer-meta-model.ts's per-rule knownLimitation field for FIGM-VUE-01/02, which carries the same correction. All 6/6 Vue rules are REAL_AST as of this revision; none remain LEGACY_TEXT_HEURISTIC. FIGM-ANG-06's fixture (Ang06Benchmark.pipe.ts) classifies as GENERIC_ESTREE, not ANGULAR_TEMPLATE, because detectFramework's Angular-hint check only recognizes @Component(...)/.component.ts, not @Pipe(...) -- this is the same GENERIC_ESTREE framework value FIGM-ANG-01/02/05 already accept. FIGM-NEXT-03 required extending EvaluationRunner's file discovery (src/eval/evaluation-runner.ts's collectTestbedFiles) from a flat readdirSync to a recursive walk, since its real-AST detector requires a literal app/<segment>/page.<ext> App Router path -- benchmarks/testbed/next03/app/demo/page.tsx is the only non-flat fixture in this testbed. All other fixtures are completely unaffected: a flat file's relative path is identical to its old bare filename. Addition (Pre-Freeze Technical Completion Pass): benchmarks/testbed/negative/ (21 files, discovered automatically by collectTestbedFiles' recursive walk) adds genuine NEGATIVE/CLEAN fixtures for 21 of the 50 rules -- a representative sample across all three research domains (6 Architecture, 8 Static Performance, all 7 Accessibility rules), not a mechanical 'remove the trigger token' transform of the existing positive fixtures but independently-written, realistic compliant code (e.g. FIGM-PERF-01's negative hoists the allocation to a frozen module-level constant; FIGM-REACT-03's negative uses a real functional state update via the setter). None of these 21 files has a corresponding entry in groundTruthViolations below -- by the same exact-match logic EvaluationRunner already uses to compute FP, any diagnostic FIGM raises on a file with no ground-truth entry is automatically counted as a false positive, so no schema change or new evaluation-runner logic was needed to make these count. Each was individually verified via a direct RuleExecutionEngine.analyzeFile call to genuinely produce zero FIGM diagnostics before being added (several iterations were needed: some initial drafts incidentally co-fired FIGM-PERF-05 (an inline JSX arrow-function handler) or FIGM-A11Y-07 (an aria-label not containing its element's visible text) and were rewritten, e.g. by wrapping handlers in useCallback -- the same real remediation this project's own rules recommend -- rather than by weakening the fixture's realism). Re-running EvaluationRunner with these 21 files included still reports FP=0 across the full 50-rule set -- a genuine, not assumed, result: the controlled benchmark's TP=65/FP=0/FN=0 was not touched or forced, it is what EvaluationRunner actually computed after the addition. This meaningfully improves (without fully resolving) the benchmark's most-cited validity limitation: the original 46-fixture corpus contained zero true-negative examples, so a 100% precision figure demonstrated only that positive fixtures fire correctly, never that FIGM stays quiet on genuinely compliant code. 21/50 rules now have at least one verified negative fixture; 29/50 do not yet -- this is a partial, not complete, remedy, and should be described as such.
